answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation slow and non-transferable: each identity earns standing only from a long public history of completed exchanges with distinct counterparties, and standing decays if it goes quiet. A fresh identity starts with no ivory-tower privilege, zero trust, and must do real verifiable work for weeks to earn any, while a whisper of complaint from several counterparties freezes it. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must sustain a thousand long honest histories, like growing timber, which costs far more than the fraud is worth.
